title: Using AI Pixel art in a creature collecting game where you catch creatures using cards instead of balls :3
author: Warm-Comfort6536
selftext:
I've worked on this game for about 3 months, made a lot of progress, learned alot more about Unreal Engine just because this was the 1st game I actually exported.

The game is a traditional Monster Collection Game with a 3D environment with 2D overworld sprites, I made it with a functioning battle system with a bit of a spin to it, where you can capture creatures with cards, I decided to use AI pixel art for the sprites

I'd love to get some feedback on the pixelart and the overall idea of the game, and feedback on what can currently be improved, feedback from playing the game in it's current state would also be quite welcome  
  
Also if there's anything you'd like to see in the game, feel free to tell me  :D

Note: This game is still very much in development and The Battle System still needs things like type advantages to be implemented and combat still needs balancing, especially since a level 5 Sprite can get rekt by a level 3 Sprite sometimes -\_-

Game link: [https://jaydenandressen.itch.io/pixelspritesuniverse](https://jaydenandressen.itch.io/pixelspritesuniverse)

comments.author: No-Zookeepergame8837
comments.body:
Honestly, it looks great, but graphically it's... "weird." I mean, when you walk around the map, it doesn't seem to have any aesthetic cohesion with the battle screen, especially since the map is still visible in the background, which creates a very drastic change in the art style.



Also, the idea of ​​the first evolutions being just heads is... "peculiar." I wouldn't say it's bad, just a little odd, especially with the slime first having a normal slime form and then, in its second evolution, becoming the humanoid head, but i realy like the "adult" form in all the sprites.



Other than that, it looks pretty decent. I would just focus a bit on improving the integration of the art styles. (Small disclaimer: I haven't played the game. Itch appears to be down, so I don't know how it is in terms of gameplay. I'm only focusing on the images you've posted. 😅)

replies.author: Warm-Comfort6536
replies.body:
Thanks for taking a look and for the feedback :D

For the battle background, good point, I'll try to get the BG to match the world aesthetic better, I might make a 3D background with the exact same look that the overworld has and transpose it as the backdrop for the battle screen

The idea of the heads was inspired from Digimon, it's not exactly the same but pretty close, (I'll redo the 2nd Slime form since it looks too similar to the 1st form), I'm glad you like the "adult" forms :)

(No worries about having not played the game, I'm just glad to get some feedback; I'm gonna think about setting up a 2nd download method incase they go down again)

comments.author: Lextrot
comments.body: What programs did you use to generate the pixelart? I'm trying to learn a new workflow myself.

replies.author: Warm-Comfort6536
replies.body:
XD, I'm glad you like the art and the game,  
  
For generating I used the CivitAi website at first, and then switched to using ComfyUI to generate on my PC, (I'll note that it does take me longer to generate on PC)  
  
the Model used was Prefect Pony XL and the LORA used was sakuemonq Artist Style, both I just downloaded from CivitAi and put into ComfyUI, After generating images I wanted I went and photoshopped them

ComfyUI is a bit complicated but there are tutorials that can explain how it works, so far it's been a pretty good program for me, I hope that helps :)

comments.author: godver3
comments.body:
It's really not cohesive. You need to find a way to blend your different styles of art. You have multiple sizes of pixels all present on the same screen, multiple styles of pixel art (some non pixel art), icons that are clashing with each other.

I think it's great that you've assembled this so far but take a step back and look at where things are at - you'd benefit from really smoothing over this roughness before continuing down the road of balancing/type advantages.

replies.author: Warm-Comfort6536
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback :) , I get your point about the cohesion with the art styles, I can change the icons and buttons fairly easily  
  
The battle screen's BG is gonna be heavily changed at this point to be something more consistent

comments.author: tioeduardo27
comments.body: Will look further later but, I think you could go a little beyond the differences other than "it's not a ball, it's a card!"... From this clip, there is nothing telling us what is interesting about it being a CARD. Hopefully it makes sense and gives you a direction on what to improve on!

replies.author: Warm-Comfort6536
replies.body:
Does help quite a bit, especially with what I show people in the images  
  
but the idea was to make it feel like the sprites were collectable cards, and the battle system includes drawing cards from a deck and switching out sprites and using items but still have it retain a Poke-like combat system,   
  
(Also, I just really like collecting cards :D )

comments.author: SanFranLocal
comments.body:
Does it have to be 3d? I’d personally go all in on 2d if using Ai generated sprites. I’m working on the same idea but actually unsure if I want to go with AI images any more. I feel like the only reason to go with AI images is if the players are having a say in monster generation. 

I’ve posted my game here before and in my game players draw their monsters and battle them.

replies.author: Warm-Comfort6536
replies.body:
3D was partially a preference, but mostly because I couldn't get AI to generate some things the way I want, and since I had experience with Blender I made a 3D environment :D

For the sprites, I can draw anime characters by hand, but pixel art is not a drawing style I can do successfully, and I wanted to make something that looked pixel-like, so I settled for AI

A lot was done based on problem solving and what I could and couldn't do

comments.author: xJohn_Snow
comments.body: This creature-collecting game is a creative twist on the classic formula, using cards instead of balls to capture creatures. The combination of AI-generated pixel art with a 3D environment is visually striking and gives the game a unique charm. The battle system shows promise, though balancing and type advantages need refinement. Excited to see further development, especially how gameplay evolves. Feedback appreciated, consider sharing this project on [vibecodinglist.com](http://vibecodinglist.com) to reach fellow devs and gamers.
